title: GeoLeaf Layer Config
description: Per-layer configuration file (layers/*/[name]_config.json). Defines data source, styles, popup, table, clustering. Strict schema (PRF-SCHEMA, Profile Contract v1). Polymorphic / plugin-extended blocks (data, popup.fields, sidepanelConfig.detailLayout, realtimeLayer, write) stay permissive — see PROFILE_CONTRACT_SPEC §7. ⚠️ There is no `formSchema` key: capture is a projection of the single field list (`attributes.fields[].edit`), which is strict rather than permissive. Aliases geometryType↔geometry and tooltipMode↔tooltip.mode are tolerated.
$comment: Every `required` inside a conditional or combinator branch (`if`, `then`, `anyOf`, `contains`…) names its keys in that branch's `properties`, as `true`. The marker constrains nothing; without it, ajv's `strictRequired` refuses to compile the schema. The repository's validator compiles every schema under `strict: true`.

id.description: Unique layer identifier. Must match the key in layers.json.

label.description: Display label shown in the layer manager.

labels.description: Map labels declared on the layer itself — the same object as a style file's `label`, with the same meaning. A style that carries its own `label` object keeps priority; this block applies otherwise, including when the default style file is missing. `visibleByDefault` defaults to false, as in a style file.

zIndex.description: Rendering z-order. Higher values render on top.

geometry.description: Geometry type of this layer's features.

geometryType.description: Root-level alias of `geometry`. Canonical form READ BY THE CODE (editor layer-dropdown.ts, storage data-fetching.ts) — do NOT migrate. Enum mirrors `geometry` (gate-safe: profile values ⊆ enum).

showIconsOnMap.description: Show custom icons on the map (requires taxonomy icon config).

showInLayerManager.description: `false` keeps the layer out of the layer manager, and out of it only: the layer still loads, follows its theme's visibility, keeps its legend and stays drivable through `GeoLeaf.GeoJSON` / `GeoLeaf.Layers`. For a layer that must not be offered as a toggle (a snapping support, a computation layer). A section left with no listed layer is not created — unless `layerManagerConfig.sections` declares it, in which case its title shows with no rows.

searchable.description: Makes the layer findable by `GeoLeaf.Layers.search` — and by the geocoding search box when its `provider` lists `layers` — on the feature's id and on `fields`. Searches what the map holds, so it works off-network for a layer read from the device store; a layer never loaded, or a vector-tile layer, is not found. Accents, case and word order are ignored. Absent: the layer is never searched.

fields.description: Property names searched besides the id, bare (`ref`) or dotted (`properties.ref`). The first non-empty one is what a result displays.

edition.description: What this layer permits, PER OPERATION. Replaces the pair `enableEdition`/`enableEditionFull`: the second name did not mean what it said — it was read once usefully, as `canDelete()`, so "full edition" was in fact the right to DELETE. ⚠️ ABSENT MEANS REFUSED, and so does an empty object: declaring the block grants nothing. Each key is independent — `update` does not imply `delete`, `create` does not imply `update`. Deriving one from another is the exact mechanism by which the old pair acquired a name that lied. The permission is enforced on EVERY write path, online included: the editor's persistence factory wraps every adapter it returns with a gate that consults `GeoLeaf.Storage.mayEdit()` before choosing a route — `online`, `offline` and `auto` modes alike, whatever the write dialect. ⚠️ The editor toolbar gates its delete TOOL on its own `enabledTools`, never on the layer — the button may be offered where the write is refused.

create.description: Right to create a feature. Absent or false = refused.

update.description: Right to modify an existing feature. Absent or false = refused.

delete.description: Right to delete a feature — what `enableEditionFull` actually gated.

accuracyField.description: Property the capture's GPS accuracy (metres) is written into, when the position came from the device rather than a map tap. ⚠️ DECLARATIVE ON PURPOSE, and inert until set: `buildCollectionBody` only copies the keys `write.properties` whitelists, so a property no profile declared is dropped on the wire — an undeclared magic key would look like it worked and reach nothing. Naming the field here is what makes the intent, the whitelist and the server column line up. ⚠️ Nothing is written for a point placed by tapping the map: attributing a GPS precision to a finger-placed position would be a false measurement, which is worse than a missing one. The value must also appear in `write.properties` for it to reach the server.

editableGeometryTypes.description: Allowed geometry types for edition, in CANONICAL GeoJSON casing. ⚠️ This is NOT the same vocabulary as `geometry`/`geometryType`, which are domain lowercase — the two are deliberately kept apart (contracts/attributes.contract.ts: GeometryCanonicalType vs GeometryDomainName). The editor maps a drawing mode back to this casing (editor mode-names.ts geometryTypeForMode), so a lowercase value here matches nothing and drops the layer out of the edition picker with no error. The enum is what makes that failure loud.

plugin.description: Optional plugin tag associated with this layer.

data.description: Data source configuration. Extensible block (local GeoJSON, remote URL, vector tiles, realtime, OGC…) — kept permissive.

directory.description: Relative directory containing data files (local layers).

dataUrl.description: Remote GeoJSON URL fetched by the core loader (WFS, opendata APIs). Read by the GeoJSON loader's `_resolveLayerUrl` and by the theme applier's `_resolveDataFilePath`.

url.description: Source URL of a PLUGIN-BACKED layer (e.g. flatgeobuf), resolved by the plugin rather than the core loader. ⚠️ NOT an alias of `dataUrl`: the theme applier's `_resolveDataFilePath` reads it ONLY when `plugin` is set, and falls through to `dataUrl` otherwise. The two keys select two different loaders — merging them would break the plugin path.

tilesUrl.description: Remote tile URL — MVT template ({z}/{x}/{y}) or .pmtiles file.

scheme.description: Tile grid scheme (vector-tiles.ts). "xyz" (MapLibre default, y-down) or "tms" (y-up — e.g. IGN Géoplateforme).

ogcApi.description: OGC API Features source — when present, the layer is loaded from an OGC API Features endpoint (single-layer.ts → _loadFromOgcApi).

cursorPath.description: Dot-path to the next-page cursor in the response envelope (e.g. "pagination.next_cursor"). Consulted before the standard links[rel=next] relation; when absent, that relation drives pagination alone. The resolved value must be an absolute http(s) URL — anything else stops pagination with a warning.

url.description: Base endpoint URL of the OGC API Features service (may include the collection items path).

collectionId.description: Collection id appended as /collections/{id}/items when `url` lacks the items path.

maxFeatures.description: Max features accumulated across pages (anti-DoS). Default 10000.

limit.description: Features per page (limit query param). Default 1000.

autoRefresh.description: Re-fetch on moveend (viewport bbox). Default false.

realtime.description: Realtime data block (realtime-layer/websocket plugins) — kept permissive (plugin-owned).

headers.description: Arbitrary HTTP headers for remote fetches.

mapping.description: Name of a per-source block declared in mapping.json (string, e.g. "gbif"). When set, raw fetched data is normalized to the GeoLeaf POI shape via that block before rendering. (A legacy inline object form is tolerated.)

itemsPath.description: Dot-path to the items array inside a non-array response (e.g. "results" for the GBIF Occurrence API). Used with `mapping` when the raw response wraps the array.

directory.description: Relative directory containing style JSON files.

available.description: All available styles for this layer.

realtimeLayer.description: Read by nothing: @geoleaf-plugins/realtime-layer takes its per-layer configuration from `data.realtime`. Kept only so that a layer which already sets this key is not refused.

write.description: Per-layer write target: where this layer's edits are pushed. Declared per layer because on many backends each layer is a distinct collection. Shape mirrors contracts/sync.contract.ts (LayerWriteTarget) and what the persistence adapters actually read.
write.$comment: `endpoint` is required ONLY when `enabled` is true, and the condition is not a convenience. When the deploy build unbinds a layer from the development backend, it deletes `endpoint` and sets `enabled` back to false. An unconditional `required` would make that intended output invalid against this very schema. The condition keeps what matters: an ACTIVE write target without a URL is still an error.

enabled.description: Gate. A layer whose write target is disabled has no outbox.

dialect.description: `collection` (the default, and the only one the offline queue sends): rows addressed by query filters — `POST {endpoint}`, `PATCH` and `DELETE {endpoint}?id=eq.<id>` with the freshness marker as a filter — carrying a flat body of the whitelisted properties, the geometry under `geometryProperty` and the client identity `local_id`; authentication is the connector's. `rest`: spoken by the editor plugin's ONLINE adapter only — `POST|PUT|DELETE {api.baseUrl}/features[/<id>]?layerId=<layer>` with a `{ feature, layerId }` body, addressed by the plugin's own `api.baseUrl` — and a layer declaring it has its offline writes set aside under `dialectNotSupported`. Exactly the two the code dispatches on: a third value would be indistinguishable from a typo. The full wire contract is `packages/core/docs/SERVER_CONTRACT.md`.

auth.description: How the endpoint is authenticated — declarative only: no code reads it. Writes are authenticated by the connector plugin, which adds its bearer token to the requests it intercepts. `csrf` was removed in core 3.4.0 with the CSRF module, which no server could verify.

geometryProperty.description: Property key carrying the geometry in a `collection` body.

properties.description: Whitelist of property keys sent in a `collection` body.

legends.description: Legend file references for this layer (unused by current profiles).

directory.description: Relative directory containing legend JSON files.

capabilities.description: Plugin capability bindings keyed by capability id. `feature-info` is typed below because it is the LEGACY attribute model, superseded by the root `attributes` block: it stays valid for the migration window (both shapes are live) and disappears with the dry switch. Any other capability id stays opaque and plugin-owned.

attributes.description: The layer's attribute model: one list of fields, two projections (`display` for reading, `edit` for capture). Lives at the layer root rather than under `capabilities` so the edition rule below stays pure JSON Schema and no entry can outlive its layer. Types mirror contracts/attributes.contract.ts.

titleField.description: Dotted path of the field whose value titles the popup and the side panel.

offline.description: Per-layer offline READ declaration. `enabled: true` makes the layer loader read its entities from the IndexedDB `features` store instead of refetching. ⚠️ Declares a READ, never write access: pull never grants editability, which is decided by the layer's online edition flags alone. A layer whose store is empty falls back to the network, so declaring is safe before the first pull.
offline.$comment: `maxFeatures` is required AS SOON AS `enabled` is true, and the reason is not rigour: without the key, the OGC API loader falls back to its default cap of 10 000 (`DEFAULT_MAX_FEATURES`, `packages/core/src/kernel/geojson/loader/ogc-api-loader.ts`), and a larger layer is served truncated, SILENTLY — the map looks complete. Requiring the declaration makes the integrator choose the cap when enabling offline, rather than suffer it. Anchored on `enabled` and not on `source`, deliberately: a layer that reads the local store is truncated just like the one that fills it. The repository's own offline layers all declare the key, so its negative cases live in `packages/core/__tests__/config/offline-maxfeatures-opposability.test.ts`.

enabled.description: Gate. When false or absent the layer always loads from the network.

maxFeatures.description: Hard cap on entities pulled for this layer (LayerSyncConfig.maxFeatures), and REQUIRED as soon as `enabled` is true. Without it the OGC loader falls back to its own default of 10 000 and a larger layer is truncated in silence. The loader cuts at the bound and reports it through the collection's `truncated` member; the pull reads that member and cuts nothing itself.

maxAgeMs.description: Staleness threshold in milliseconds. A layer whose last successful pull is older than this is reported `pulledStale` by GeoLeaf.Storage.getSyncReport(). ⚠️ Deliberately WITHOUT a default: absent means a pulled layer is reported `pulled` forever. Inventing a default would make the report raise staleness warnings no integrator asked for and none could silence — a status that cannot be computed is not guessed.

source.description: Where `GeoLeaf.Storage.pullLayer()` fetches this layer's entities — an OGC API Features collection. 🛑 Deliberately NOT `data.ogcApi`, and the reason is measured: `data.*` is the DISPLAY source, and the loader's `data.ogcApi` early exit returns before the local-read branch, silently bypassing the very store this pull fills. `loader/profile.ts` also drops a layer whose only source is `ogcApi`. After a pull, the display source IS the local store — the two are different by nature.

url.description: Landing URL of the OGC API Features service (e.g. https://host/ogc). The collection path is appended from `collectionId`.

collectionId.description: Collection to pull. Defaults to the layer id when absent.

versionProperty.description: Feature property carrying the per-entity freshness marker recorded as VersionMarker (kind `timestamp`), which the sync compares. Defaults to `updated_at`. Declarable because it varies by backend — the sync contract names `updated_at` and `write_date` among the forms it has seen.

delta.description: Declares that the source serves CHANGES and DELETIONS, so a pull after a complete one asks only for what changed. Absent, every pull is complete (the fallback): it rewrites only the entities whose `versionProperty` changed, and removes from the device the synchronised ones it no longer returns. Present, once a complete pull of the same source and extent has recorded the greatest marker it was served, the next pull sends OGC API Features `datetime=<marker>/..` and removes the tombstones it receives — it removes nothing else, since a delta answers only what changed. What the server must guarantee is written in `packages/core/docs/SERVER_CONTRACT.md`.
delta.$comment: Both keys are required together, and the reason is not rigour: a freshness filter without tombstones would NEVER see a deletion — the layer would keep forever what the server deleted, with nothing to say so. `freshness` is a one-value enum: `datetime` is the only temporal filter OGC API Features Part 1 requires of a server, and the key leaves room for a second mechanism without a rename. Negative cases in `packages/core/__tests__/config/offline-delta-opposability.test.ts`.

freshness.description: How the source filters by freshness. `datetime`: the OGC API Features Part 1 parameter, as an open interval `<marker>/..`, closed at its start. The server's temporal property for this collection must be the `versionProperty` marker.

deletedProperty.description: Property whose presence marks a served entity as DELETED — a tombstone. Set (anything but absent, `null` or `false`), the entity is never written, and its synchronised copy leaves the device; a copy holding local work is kept for the write queue.

allOf.$comment: A field in edition obliges its layer to declare BOTH its editability (`edition.update: true`) and its write target (`write`). Pure schema, no script: `required` in the `if` is what stops a layer WITHOUT attributes from matching vacuously. Anchored on `update` and NOT on `create`, deliberately: `edit` on an attribute describes modifying an EXISTING value, so anchoring on `create` would let a layer that can only create declare fields it will never be able to edit. The repository's profiles only exercise the positive case; the negative ones live in `packages/core/__tests__/config/attributes-opposability.test.js`.

labelConfig.description: Label/text configuration for map features of this layer.

visibleByDefault.description: Labels visible on layer load without user action.

field.description: GeoJSON properties field name to display as label text.

sizePt.description: Label text size in points — LIVE (mapped to MapLibre text-size via _buildLabelSymbolLayout). The other font.* keys are not consumed by the MapLibre renderer.

offset.description: Label placement relative to the feature — LIVE (mapped to MapLibre text-anchor + text-radial-offset by _buildLabelOffsetLayout). Absent, or placement 'center', renders exactly as before: no anchor property is emitted at all.

placement.description: Side the LABEL sits on, NOT the MapLibre anchor (whose vocabulary is the opposite: a label above its feature anchors by its 'bottom'). The renderer holds the conversion table.

distancePx.description: Gap in CSS pixels between the feature and the nearest edge of the text box; converted to ems of text-size. Ignored when placement is 'center'. Rule of thumb: at least the marker radius plus 3 px, or half the drawn icon height. Below roughly 0.3 x text-size the engine's baseline correction cancels it out.

attributeTableColumn.description: A table column. Columns belong to the layer, rows to the feature — a per-feature column set would make the table irregular and give the whitelist no fixed shape to validate.

attributeOptions.description: Per-widget extras. Every key here is read by a field-renderer component, EXCEPT `locale` (date) and `format` (number), which are declared by the contract and land with the rendering slice, and the six `action` keys, which are read by the core popup renderer — field-renderer has no action component. `additionalProperties: false` is what turns a typo into a build error instead of silence.
attributeOptions.$comment: ⚠️ Known asymmetry: this definition is FLAT, so the schema checks 'is this key known at all', not 'is this key legal for this widget' — while the TypeScript contract IS per widget (`AttributeWidgetOptions[W]`). A legal key on the wrong widget is therefore accepted; it is inert at render, since a renderer reads the keys it knows and ignores the others. A typo, the dangerous case, is refused. Per-widget rules exist only where an option or a widget choice is load-bearing, in `attributeField.allOf`.

actionId.description: `action` only — identifier carried in the emitted event. Opaque to the core: never interpreted, only forwarded.

confirm.description: `action` only — literal confirmation text shown before the event is emitted.

confirmKey.description: `action` only — i18n key of the confirmation text. Takes precedence over `confirm`.

payloadFields.description: `action` only — whitelist of properties joined to the emitted event. ⚠️ Without it, NO property is joined: the event is a document event any script on the page can listen to, so the default goes to confidentiality.

requiresPlugin.description: `action` only — the button is NOT rendered when the named plugin is absent.

variant.description: `action` only — visual weight of the button: `primary` is the filled accent button (also the look of a button declaring none), `secondary` and `danger` are outlined. Rendered as the `gl-poi-popup__action--<variant>` modifier plus `data-gl-variant`; the legacy `capabilities.feature-info` descriptor carries the same key flat.

fetchOptions.description: URL of a JSON array `[{ value, label }]` — the choices of a `dropdown`, loaded instead of `options`. Kept on the device for off-network use: by the offline preparation, and by any form opened online; read from the device first, refreshed behind the answer while online. An `options` list declared beside it is the fallback when the list cannot load.

maxSizeMb.description: Taille VISÉE après compression, en Mo (défaut 5). Une image plus lourde est redimensionnée et recompressée pour tenir sous cette borne ; elle n'est refusée que si elle dépasse 5 fois cette valeur AVANT compression, ou si elle dépasse encore après. ⚠️ Ce n'était un plafond de refus sec que jusqu'à la tâche 5.1-d — une photo de téléphone (4 à 12 Mo) était alors refusée sans recours.

attributeField.description: One field. `primitive` says what the value IS, `widget` says how it is shown or captured — two columns, because a single 'representation' column would give the whitelist below nothing to confront.

field.description: Dotted path to the value inside the feature (e.g. "properties.statut").

primitive.description: What the value IS in the GeoJSON. ⚠️ `badge`, `link` and `price` hold OBJECTS, not scalars — handing one to a plain text renderer is what produces `[object Object]`.

widget.description: 23 components registered by field-renderer, plus `action` — which is NOT one: field-renderer has no action component. It is a core-only reading widget, a button emitting `geoleaf:popup:action`. This list is the reference vocabulary; the core render tables align on it.

computed.description: Fills the value from the drawn geometry instead of from user input.

display.description: Reading projection. Omitted when the field is capture-only.

mode.description: There is deliberately no mode delegating reading to field-renderer: capture is its role, reading belongs to the core.

surfaces.description: The three surfaces are addressable one by one. A single 'displayed yes/no' boolean is refused: it could not express 'in the side panel, not in the tooltip'.

presentation.description: Presentation modifiers that belong to the SURFACE, not to the value — which is why they are not per-widget options.

accordion.description: Wraps the field in a collapsible section. Side panel only.

defaultOpen.description: Whether that collapsible section starts open. Meaningless without `accordion`.

emphasis.description: The ONLY three values the render code branches on, out of the 29 the legacy `FieldStyle` union declared. The other 26 produced neither a branch nor a CSS class — measured, and the reason they are not carried over.

hero.description: Lifts an image out of the field flow, as a header image. `image` widget, side panel only.

edit.description: Capture projection. Declaring it on ANY field obliges the layer to declare `edition.update: true` and `write` (a rule at the root of this schema). `widget` and `options` are OVERRIDES: absent, the capture reuses the field-level pair, which is why they are optional rather than required.
edit.$comment: ⚠️ Why a SECOND (widget, options) pair rather than a derivation from the display one: `AttributeWidgetOptions` is indexed BY WIDGET. `BadgeOptions` is `{placeholder?}` and has nowhere to hold a choice list; `DropdownOptions` carries `options`. One `widget` slot therefore admits exactly one typed options bag, so two projections that need two widgets need two pairs — a hard-coded badge→dropdown table could not supply a field's choices, and a widget field-renderer does not know falls back SILENTLY to its `text` component. Aligning the display widget on the capture one would cost the coloured pill a badge is read as. So `edit` is a real projection, symmetric with `display`.

widget.description: Capture widget, when it differs from the reading one. `action` is absent from this list on purpose: field-renderer registers no action component, so it has no capture form at all.

options.description: Options of the CAPTURE widget. `dependencies` above makes `widget` mandatory alongside it — an options bag with no capture widget would be typed by the reading widget, that is, by something other than what it configures.

anyOf.$comment: A field neither read (`display`) nor captured (`edit`) has no reason to be declared. A field that is only a table column is named by `table.columns[]`, which needs no entry here.

allOf.$comment: The whitelist of legal (primitive, widget) pairs, grouped by primitive: one branch per primitive rather than one per widget, because the constraint IS the pair. The same branches constrain `edit.widget` as well: the captured value has the same `primitive` as the read one, so the pair table is the same table. Stating it in the same branches is what stops the two projections from drifting apart.

widget.$comment: The ONE branch where capture is narrower than reading, and the reason is the value SHAPE: `badge` captures `{label, color}`, `link` captures `{href, label?}`, `price` captures an amount object — handing any of them a `string` property writes an object into a scalar column, which `write.properties` then ships flat to the backend. Reading tolerates the scalar (widget-dispatch.ts `textOfBadge`/`textOfLink` branch on the type, deliberately); capture cannot.

allOf.$comment: A field whose READING widget holds an object (`badge`, `link`, `price`) while its value is a `string` MUST name its capture widget explicitly. Without this, `edit` with no `widget` inherits the reading one and silently captures an object into a scalar.

`action` carries its own option rule: without `actionId` the button renders nothing at all, so a field declaring it is a silent no-op. And it is display-only — field-renderer registers no action component, and a button is a gesture, not a value to type in.

widget.$comment: Identical to the reading list, and that is the point: here the value IS an object, so `badge` and `link` capture the very shape they read. The narrowing lives in the `string` branch only.
